title: Unstructured eval incubation pad - Aarav
content:
Context: quick personal incubation space. Trying to capture a few odd regression signals from the last week of Canary for rn-model-v2 (hosted). Not polished — intentionally messy. Use this as a scratchpad and single-source-of-truth for the tiny experiments I keep re-running before I formalize as a reproducible test in the eval harness.

Goals and framing:
- Capture small, reproducible prompt/response pairs that show subtle quality regressions after quantization/kv-cache change.
- Build a micro-rubric I can use to triage whether the failure is correctness vs. phrasing vs. non-deterministic sampling noise.
- Quick filters to prioritize which samples go to the nightly regression alarm.

Hypotheses to test (short):
1) New dynamic kv-cache boundary logic causes token truncation for prompts with long preambles (likely off-by-one).
2) Quantization profile `q4_0_lowmem` slightly increases hallucination rate on list-generation tasks (narrow scope).
3) Beam/temperature tuning interplay: small temperature changes cause inconsistent slot-filling when prefix tokens are repeated.

Mini ad-hoc rubric (for this pad only) — header + scores 0/1/2: 
- Faithfulness (0: wrong fact / 1: partial / 2: accurate)
- Instruction-adherence (0: ignores instruction / 1: partial / 2: follows)
- Stability (0: flaky across seeds / 1: minor variations / 2: stable)
- Truncation-risk (0: truncated / 1: edge / 2: full)
- Severity tag: blocker | annoying | informational

Quick checklist for repro steps when I move to harness:
- pin model: rn-model-v2@2025-10-23
- set quant profile: q4_0_lowmem vs q8_0_ref
- run seeds: 7, 11, 23 (deterministic where possible)
- enable/disable dynamic-kv-cache toggle (runtime flag: enable_dynamic_kv = true/false)
- run with both streaming enabled/disabled (client vs server)

Sample set A: long preamble + slot fill (possible kv cache truncation)
Prompt (P1): "System: You are a concise assistant. User: I have a long meeting note preamble followed by an explicit request. [PASTED 480 tokens of meeting notes...] Now summarize the three action items for the engineering team, numbered."

Observed (seed 11, q4_0_lowmem, enable_dynamic_kv=true):
- Output (trimmed): "1) Add backlog prioritization; 2) ..., 3) ..." (note: output ends mid-sentence at item 2)
Micro-rubric: Faithfulness=1, Instruction-adherence=1, Stability=0, Truncation-risk=0, Severity=blocker
Notes: output seems cut at a predictable token boundary when preamble > ~450 tokens. Repeatable across two runs. With dynamic_kv off the response completes. Suspect kv cache eviction or incorrect copy of prefix length. File a unit test that simulates long prefix > 450 tokens with continuous attention.

Sample set B: enumerated list hallucination (quant profile suspected)
Prompt (P2): "List five common causes of delayed jobs in distributed ingestion pipelines (brief bullets)."

Observed variants: 
- q4_0_lowmem (seed 7): returned five bullets but third bullet incorrectly attributes root cause to "deprecated network protocol XZ-1" (doesn't exist in our infra).
- q8_0_ref (seed 7): returned credible bullets (backpressure, rate limiting, slow consumers, GC pauses, retries).

Micro-rubric per-run: q4: Faithfulness=0, Instr-adherence=2, Stability=1, Truncation=2, Severity=annoying
Notes: looks like lower-bit quantization correlates with spurious factual insertions on taxonomy-style items. Need to expand sample space to other taxonomy prompts (security control lists, compliance checklist) to see correlation.

Sample set C: repeated prefix token instability (temperature interplay)
Prompt (P3): "Rewrite the following clause to be more neutral and concise: "The board emphatically believes that all stakeholders are fully responsible for ensuring the integrity of the ledger, and anyone found otherwise will face disciplinary action." Provide 3 variants."

Observed: temperature 0.2 produced 3 highly similar variants (OK). Temperature 0.7 produced one variant that inserted a new clause referencing a "remote audit agent" (hallucination). Lower temperature + beam=3 stabilizes.
Micro-rubric: Faithfulness=2, Instr-adherence=2, Stability=0, Truncation=2, Severity=informational
Notes: ambiguous instruction plus mid-temp sampling can introduce stray invented entities. Consider lowering default temp for rewrite workflows where inventing is costly.

Quick experiments I ran this morning (results):
- Re-run P1 on q8_0_ref: completes successfully. => suggests kv-cache + quant combo.
- Re-run P1 with enable_dynamic_kv=false on q4_0_lowmem: completes successfully. => dynamic_kv path likely root cause when combined with q4 profile.
- Re-run P2 on a small battery of 10 taxonomy prompts: 3/10 show spurious-named-thing hallucinations on q4_0_lowmem, 0/10 on q8_0_ref.

Immediate actions (next 48h):
- Create a minimal unit test that reproduces the P1 truncation locally and add to serving-runtime tests (ticket JIRA-MLINF-334).
- Add a 10-sample taxonomy test to the nightly regression suite comparing q4_0_lowmem vs q8_0_ref (low cost).
- Disable the q4_0_lowmem rollout for hosted API customers in Canary region until triage (temp mitigation). Ops notification draft: slack #infra-ops @oncall.

Longer term ideas (parking lot):
- Add a deterministic mode for dynamic_kv where eviction thresholds are conservative for long-prefix prompts.
- Augment quantization profile metadata with empirical hallucination likelihood by task category (embedding, taxonomy, list, rewrite).
- Build a small fuzz harness that stresses repeated-token prefixes and measures divergence across seeds and quant profiles.

Questions I still have / to check: 
- Is there a correlation between sequence length distribution during beam expansion and the cache eviction formula? (ask runtime folks: PR #412 touches kernel selection code)
- Do we have any telemetry that links cases of truncated outputs to specific GC or OOM events on GPU? (need SRE help)
- Is the q4_0_lowmem profile compiled with an updated kernel set that interplays poorly with dynamic kv? (compare build tags)

Notes to self for turning this into a formal eval doc:
- Keep this set as the seed: P1 (long preamble), P2 (taxonomy list), P3 (rewrite). Expand to 20 more prompts with similar structure.
- When moving to eval-harness, add explicit token-level diffs and earliest-truncation-index metric.
- Decide alarm threshold: e.g., >2/10 taxonomy prompts with hallucinations => regression alert.

Scratch experiments / quick snippets I tried: 
- Small script: curl hosted-api/call -H 'X-Model: rn-model-v2@2025-10-23' --data '{"prompt":"P1...","quant":"q4_0_lowmem","seed":11,"flags":{"dynamic_kv":true}}' | jq '.completion'
- Grep logs for "kv-evict" entries around 2025-11-03 02:10Z — saw repeated eviction events coincident with the truncations.

Final quick mental model: combination of kv cache boundary logic plus memory-conservative quantization increases odds of early truncation and occasional hallucination on taxonomy tasks. Likely fix: either conservative cache eviction when dynamic mode is enabled or fallback to q8 on long prefixes until we iron out kernel interactions.

If anyone reads: ping me in slack @aarav with any pointers or if you want to pair-run the unit test. Will convert to a formal reproducible test and PR if behavior is stable across CI.
